# WWI Policy (Sample — Toy Demo, 2 Pages)

> **This is a sample policy for the training demo only.** It deliberately contains the rules and edge cases the evaluation set tests. It is not a real corporate policy.

## Section 1 — Scope

This policy covers business travel booked through the WWI agent for all full-time employees. Contractors must use the contractor-travel workflow (not covered here).

## Section 2 — Booking window

- Domestic trips: book at least **7 days** in advance unless an emergency travel exception is approved.
- International trips: book at least **21 days** in advance.
- Exceptions require manager + travel-ops approval.

## Section 3 — Per-trip budget caps

| Trip type | Default cap (USD) |
|---|---|
| Domestic, 1–2 nights | $1,200 |
| Domestic, 3+ nights | $2,000 |
| International, 1–3 nights | $2,500 |
| International, 4+ nights | $3,500 |

Caps include flight + hotel + ground transport. Exceeding a cap requires VP approval (over by ≤15%) or CFO approval (over by >15%).

## Section 4 — Reimbursable categories

### 4.1 — Ground transport
Taxi, rideshare, train, and rental car economy/intermediate class are reimbursable. Luxury class rental requires manager approval.

### 4.2 — Parking
Airport parking is reimbursable up to **$25/day**. Submit the receipt within **30 days** of the trip return date. Valet parking is reimbursable only when self-park is unavailable.

### 4.3 — Meals
Per-diem: **$75/day domestic, $95/day international**. Alcohol is **not** reimbursable except for approved client entertainment (Section 8).

### 4.4 — Wi-Fi and connectivity
In-flight Wi-Fi on flights ≥2 hours is reimbursable. Hotel Wi-Fi is reimbursable when not complimentary.

## Section 5 — Non-reimbursable

- Personal entertainment (movies, minibar, spa).
- Travel insurance purchased independently (WWI provides this).
- Upgrades paid in cash (mileage upgrades are fine).
- Pet boarding, childcare, or personal errands.

## Section 6 — Hotels

Use the preferred hotel partner program when available. Maximum nightly rate by city tier:

| City tier | Examples | Max nightly (USD) |
|---|---|---|
| Tier 1 | NYC, SF, London, Tokyo | $325 |
| Tier 2 | Berlin, Boston, Seattle | $235 |
| Tier 3 | All others | $185 |

Exceeding the nightly cap requires manager approval (≤20% over) or VP approval (>20% over).

## Section 7 — Flights

### 7.1 — Class of service

- **Economy** is the default for all flights.
- **Premium economy** is allowed for flights ≥6 hours.
- **Business class** is allowed only for flights >6 hours **and** requires VP approval at booking time.
- **First class** is never reimbursable.

### 7.2 — Carrier preference
Use preferred carriers when fare is within 10% of the cheapest option. Personal mileage accounts are permitted; do not book primarily to accumulate miles.

### 7.3 — Schedule constraints
Avoid arrivals after midnight local time when a morning-of meeting is scheduled. Same-day return is not required when the meeting ends after 4 PM local.

## Section 8 — Client entertainment

Meals and drinks with clients are reimbursable up to **$150/person** with itemized receipts and attendee list. Alcohol is reimbursable in this context.

## Section 9 — Receipts and submission

- All receipts ≥ $25 require itemized documentation.
- Submit within **30 days** of trip return. After 60 days, reimbursement requires VP approval and a written exception.
- Mobile photos of receipts are accepted.

## Section 10 — Exceptions

Any deviation from this policy must be documented in the expense report's notes field with the approver name. Travel-ops audits 10% of trips monthly.
